external_primary_crosschecks.note: AAAI primary abstract confirms defended KataGo agents remain vulnerable to adaptive attacks; exact worker percentages remain scoped to the paper's reported configurations.
Primary arXiv confirms adversarial prompt optimization degrades multiple defenses, code is released, and self-incrimination plus monitoring is the strongest tested combination.
Primary abstract confirms 77-100% clean-snapshot skill success with frequent chained-state stalls and near-zero end-to-end success.
Primary abstract confirms policy-dependent non-stationary observations under folding and reports 5.19x training speedup.
Primary source confirms nonparametric e-detectors with nonasymptotic false-alarm average-run-length control and near-optimal delay in specified regimes.
Primary source confirms description-length and max-information approaches for adaptive holdout reuse.
Primary source confirms post-selection correction from approximate max-information and the product-distribution/composition-order caveat.
Primary abstract reports nine judges from seven families yield only about two effective independent votes and correlated errors dominate aggregation gains.
Primary abstract confirms large-scale agentic RL with Lean/tool interaction and strong Putnam/FATE results.
Official release confirms CISPO RL, Apache-2.0/open-weight availability and reported Putnam/FATE performance.
Primary abstract confirms evaluation-free one-shot and continual Zip-on-Write compression; replay-boundary assessment remains about public artifact completeness, not method invalidity.

assessments.tested_scope: Current public DriftLens repository, historical/current wrapper code, arXiv v2 and final-paper artifact statements; no independent detector rerun.
assessments.rationale: Direct repository inspection pins the public --run_driftlens gate regression to one commit, confirms absent tracked radius-2 HDF5/output receipts and identifies the exact missing replay bundle. This is strong reproducibility-contract evidence.
limits: Does not show that the published table-producing command used the broken wrapper.
IEEE supplementary payload was not inspected; public GitHub absence is not global artifact absence.
No independent numerical reproduction of published detector results.

assessments.tested_scope: Haddouche & Sakhi 2026 Appendix C dynamic/off-policy theorem under bounded costs, current-batch conditional assumptions and its policy representation.
assessments.rationale: Primary proof gives an exact cumulative KL path term sum KL(Q_k||Q_{k-1}) with predictable previous-posterior reference and time-uniform average sequential-risk control. The theorem is direct; the proposed two-mode scheduler is not.
limits: Targets average sequential risk under changing contexts, not one final stationary policy.
Does not detect when to switch between stable and drift modes.
No autonomous-agent end-to-end validation.

assessments.tested_scope: Nonparametric e-detector false-alarm/delay guarantees plus separate dynamic off-policy theorem.
assessments.rationale: Both components have primary formal guarantees; e-detectors provide nonasymptotic false-alarm control and near-optimal delay in specified regimes, while the learner has a dynamic-risk theorem.
limits: No theorem or matched experiment validates the composed detector-to-memory-switch controller.
Monitored statistic may miss semantic drift.
Reset/recurring-regime semantics remain open.

assessments.tested_scope: Predictable previous-posterior priors verified for the Appendix-C dynamic objective only.
assessments.rationale: The update materially narrows a prior claim: learned predictable priors are directly supported in the local/dynamic product-prior construction, while the stationary all-history extension remains unproved.
limits: Do not transfer the dynamic theorem to stationary all-history reuse.
No empirical deployment result.

assessments.tested_scope: Exact product-prior KL decomposition in the dynamic theorem.
assessments.rationale: Primary proof establishes that the path-complexity term is an exact KL decomposition and martingale consequence, not merely a heuristic regularizer.
limits: Formal result only within paper assumptions.
Small local KL increments can still sum to large long-run drift.

assessments.tested_scope: Predeclared countable counterfactual test universe; fixed-candidate valid e-processes; weighted Ville/union correction for adaptive selection.
assessments.rationale: The derivation is mechanically checkable and directly repairs a concrete reused-validation memorization attack. Dwork-style description-length validity and e-process/FWER theory support the ingredients.
limits: Not a named published theorem in this exact form.
Requires complete encoding of all validation-dependent side channels.
Can be prohibitively conservative when transcript complexity is more than a few bits.

assessments.tested_scope: Selector with beta-approximate max-information k bits and fixed-candidate e-process crossing bound.
assessments.rationale: Rogers et al. directly support the max-information bad-event inflation inequality; substituting Ville's fixed-candidate crossing event yields the stated threshold conversion.
limits: Needs a valid full-selector k,beta bound.
Approximate-DP-to-max-information has product-distribution and composition-order caveats.
No matched real-agent experiment.

assessments.tested_scope: Exact validation-independent behavioral equivalence classes only.
assessments.rationale: Aggregating prior mass over exactly test-equivalent behaviors follows the weighted-union construction and aligns with behavior-space PAC-Bayes intuition, but the exact selected-eprocess quotient is a worker synthesis.
limits: Approximate or sample-only equivalence is unsupported.
No empirical power comparison against fresh audit in realistic agents.

assessments.tested_scope: KataGo defenses and adaptive adversaries under the paper's Go threat model, compute/search settings and defended snapshots.
assessments.rationale: Peer-reviewed primary study shows defenses that stop known cyclic attacks can be defeated by freshly optimized attacks, including 92% and 90% win-rate cases with attacker training compute materially below defender training. This is direct adaptive-evaluation failure evidence.
limits: Narrow Go domain; no quantitative transfer to LLM safety.
Some attack variants weaken at higher victim-search budgets.
Not a full defender-snapshot x independently-reoptimized-attacker factorial.

assessments.tested_scope: GPT-4.1/Gemini-family agent-control settings with defense-aware prompt optimization on APPS/BashArena and held-out/transfer evaluation.
assessments.rationale: Primary 2026 paper releases code and explicitly stress-tests defenses with automated adversarial prompt optimization. The paper supports the qualitative result that adaptive optimization degrades fixed monitors and that complementary self-incrimination plus monitoring is stronger than either alone.
limits: Exact per-condition percentages in the worker artifact should remain tied to the paper tables/optimization protocol.
Not prompt-injection evidence and not a universal statement that monitoring fails.
No independent replication.

assessments.tested_scope: First-party execution-edit checker repository with Python/Lean semantics, durable operation identities and restore/replacement demos.
assessments.rationale: Public runnable artifacts strengthen implementability and reproducibility of exact execution-edit checking beyond paper-only evidence.
limits: Repository describes a research prototype, not production readiness.
No evidence it improves generic agent success or checkpoint-target selection.
No independent reproduction recorded here.

assessments.tested_scope: BEHAVIOR-1K VLA skills evaluated from clean boundary snapshots versus chained terminal states.
assessments.rationale: Primary 2026 study directly measures the handoff distribution shift: selected skills achieve 77-100% success from clean snapshots while composed rollouts frequently stall and end-to-end success is near zero. The matched checkpoint comparison strongly supports successor-readiness as a distinct failure mode.
limits: Robotics/VLA scope only.
Diagnoses the failure but does not establish a generic repair mechanism.
No independent replication.

assessments.tested_scope: Long-horizon search-agent training with context folding; separated losses, consistency loss and selective-segment training.
assessments.rationale: Primary paper identifies policy-dependent observation shift and reports stable training plus 5.19x training speedup, providing both mechanism-level and quantitative evidence that folding affects the learning-state distribution.
limits: Does not show inference-time folding is harmful in general.
Worker artifact did not inspect full fold-frequency/depth ablations.
No independent replication.

assessments.tested_scope: 16-cell synthetic archive family, 1,200 evaluator-call budget, 150-500 paired replicates and controlled evaluator dependence/error sweeps.
assessments.rationale: The matched-budget design cleanly demonstrates within the synthetic model that evaluator independence and marginal quality are separate resources and that naive switching can fail under asymmetric class-conditional errors.
limits: Synthetic controller only; no real LLM-judge causal claim.
Naive LR multiplication is intentionally miscalibrated under dependence.
Absolute values across differently seeded B blocks are not directly comparable.

assessments.tested_scope: Routing criterion based on marginal class-conditional error, cross-evaluator dependence, redirected-call count, irreversibility and throughput.
assessments.rationale: C54 plus the public correlated-judge result support rejecting a one-dimensional 'judge diversity' scalar; however the proposed marginal-system-value controller is not itself tested.
limits: No real archive-routing experiment.
Requires calibrated dependence-aware evidence combination.
Class-conditional asymmetry can invalidate simple heuristics.

assessments.tested_scope: Official Astrocyte-gated associative-memory code, 850 compiled float32 trajectories, literal PyTorch spot checks and matched-seed dt sensitivity at the low-tau branch.
assessments.rationale: The worker directly localizes negative-p/NaN behavior to the public dt discontinuity above tau_p=0.01 and shows smaller scaled dt removes those events while preserving convergence fractions for matched seeds. This is strong implementation-level failure/sensitivity evidence.
limits: Compiled implementation is equation-order-equivalent but not bitwise identical to PyTorch.
Findings concern the public Euler discretization/collector, not the continuous-time mechanism.
No independent external rerun.

assessments.tested_scope: Argus commit 962cb065... pipeline-state writer and production call-site/outer-lock inventory.
assessments.rationale: Direct code inspection shows temp+os.replace prevents torn JSON but supplies no state revision/CAS/common mutation lock, while also finding the normal daemon outer pipeline lock. This precisely narrows the current risk to external/admin/direct-writer surfaces rather than claiming a normal-daemon race.
limits: No concurrent exploit was executed.
Writer inventory is not yet proven complete.
Power-loss fsync durability remains uncharacterized.

assessments.tested_scope: Proposed one-object file-backed CAS/capability/receipt mutation boundary for Argus; Snaplist PostgreSQL tests provide external exact-once precedent.
assessments.rationale: Snaplist tests directly support stale-generation fencing, privilege boundary, late-failure rollback and exact retry semantics. The Argus adaptation is coherent but remains unimplemented and untested.
limits: Database transaction evidence does not prove file-backed atomic durability.
Partial writer migration could preserve stale whole-object clobber paths.
No task-level benefit measured.

assessments.tested_scope: Seed-Prover 1.5 formal theorem proving with large-scale agentic RL, Lean/tool interaction and terminal verifier-grounded proof success.
assessments.rationale: Primary paper directly closes the broad gap: sequential tool-interleaved formal-proof behavior is trained by agentic RL and achieves strong Putnam/FATE results under stated budgets.
limits: Does not isolate a compact typed outer controller.
Binary reward lacks explicit token/$/Lean-time cost objective.
Public 1.5 directory lacks the full trainer/controller trajectory artifact.

assessments.tested_scope: Mistral Leanstral 1.5 formal proof engineering with mid-training/SFT/CISPO RL and open weights/API.
assessments.rationale: Official release reports 587/672 PutnamBench, FATE-H 87%, FATE-X 34% and an agentic proof-engineering training setup; open weights materially strengthen inspectability.
limits: Official release is not an independent replication.
No matched ablation isolates routing/control from general model improvements.
No explicit cost-aware controller objective.

assessments.tested_scope: Public Seed-Prover 1.5 and Adapt release surfaces inspected for controller/training/data reproducibility.
assessments.rationale: The artifact audit supports a practical baseline distinction: Seed-Prover has strong paper evidence but incomplete public controller/training replay; Leanstral is much more deployable; Adapt's preprint-linked artifact metadata remains insufficient.
limits: Search failure is not proof that no external artifact exists.
Reproducibility status can change with later releases.
No numerical reproduction performed.

assessments.tested_scope: One fixed AutoResearchEval task across eight model trajectories under an unchanged severe-self-critique/closure/durable-pending coding rule.
assessments.rationale: Direct trajectory coding finds 6/8 explicit qualifying severe critiques, only 1/6 fully closed, and 0/5 unresolved severe issues surviving termination as machine-actionable repair state. The fixed same-task panel is a strong failure-pattern observation.
limits: One task only; not a prevalence estimate or model ranking.
Coding is observational and not a matched intervention.
Underlying scientific truth of each report is not adjudicated.

assessments.tested_scope: Proposed invariant that all currently open severe issues must be repaired, claim-downgraded or hard-blocked before promotion.
assessments.rationale: The panel motivates an issue-ledger invariant and specifically shows that a later severe issue can reopen closure after an earlier repair, but no matched experiment tests the proposed gate.
limits: No causal evidence that the gate improves final scientific validity.
Could impose cost/false-block tradeoffs not measured here.

assessments.tested_scope: SkillZip paper and public repository for one-shot/continual compression mechanisms; 16-round LiveMath experiment chronology/replay bundle absent from inspected public tree.
assessments.rationale: Primary paper plus code strongly support the compression mechanism and continual API, while the repository audit correctly downgrades claims about independent replay of the paper's 16-round evolution trajectory.
limits: No independent reconstruction of Figure-6/final-test numbers.
Public tree does not expose accepted-patch chronology or full SkillOpt orchestration.
Structural compression is not behavioral-promotion validity.

material_high_strength: FE-073 gives peer-reviewed adaptive-attack evidence that defense success against known attacks can collapse after fresh attacker optimization.

FE-074 gives agent-control evidence that defense-aware prompt optimization increases undetected attack success while complementary internal self-report plus monitoring remains stronger than either alone.
Semantic-handoff directly separates isolated skill success from chained-state compositional success.
Seed-Prover 1.5 and Leanstral 1.5 independently establish terminal-verifier-grounded agentic RL for formal proof engineering.
Astrocyte discretization audit localizes a numerical defect to a public dt discontinuity under matched seeds and large trajectory counts.
material_scope_guards: Cross-field stable/global-history and drift/local-history guarantees remain distinct; no unified learned-prior theorem was inferred.
Evaluation prefix/max-information corrections are worker-local conversions/derivations unless explicitly covered by the cited source theorem.
C54/C55 are synthetic controller evidence and do not establish real LLM-judge routing gains.
Argus adaptation clean-os-g1-005 remains unimplemented even though source audits and Snaplist transaction tests support its invariant design.
SkillZip compression is not evidence that a behavioral patch should be promoted, and the current public tree does not independently replay the 16-round evolution chronology.
No C11 claim was upgraded to independent replication.
